open-question.question: What value does the `--milestone` flag accept: only the exact milestone directory name under `milestones/` (as `capture-milestone-principle-updates` takes its id today, verbatim with no bare-number resolution), or also a looser form such as a bare milestone number or a `milestones/`-prefixed path with or without its trailing slash?
open-question.alternative: The flag accepts only the exact milestone directory name under `milestones/` (for example `milestone_50_uniform-milestone-resolution-with-an`), used verbatim to form `milestones/<milestone_id>/`. It applies no bare-number resolution and strips no `milestones/` prefix or trailing slash, so any other spelling is simply a value that matches no directory. It is the form `capture-milestone-principle-updates` already documents ("the value is used verbatim") and `specify-milestone-starting-state` takes today, so one `<milestone_id>` means the same thing in every skill, the stated exception included. `docs/skill-reference.md` and the placeholder line in `ways-of-using-cairn.md` keep one definition, and `get-current-milestone.md` gains an input with no normalization or lookup rule to state. The caller has to type or copy the full directory name, including a slug that `define_milestone.py` truncates to five folded words (this milestone's ends in `-with-an`) and that nobody can reliably write from memory. A path copied from the pointer line or from shell completion (`milestones/milestone_50_.../`) fails rather than resolving. Whether that failure is easy to recover from depends on what the unmatched-override error line carries, which a sibling question decides.

The flag accepts the exact directory name, and also the same name with a leading `milestones/` and/or a trailing slash, which are stripped before the remainder is matched exactly against a directory name. The full pointer-style path `milestones/milestone_<N>_<slug>/` therefore resolves. There is no bare-number resolution: once the path decoration is removed, the value must still be the whole directory name. The path written in `milestones/README.md`'s pointer line, a path from shell tab completion, and the bare directory name all work, so the common copy-and-paste ways of naming a milestone succeed. The rule stays a fixed string strip with no directory listing and no ambiguity, and the result is still always exactly one named directory. The override no longer accepts exactly what `capture-milestone-principle-updates`' positional id accepts, even though that skill's Usage text ties the two together. Either capture's documented "verbatim" form and cross-reference have to be qualified as the exception, or the two forms quietly diverge. It also adds a normalization sentence that the shared procedure (or wherever flag parsing is stated, a sibling question) has to carry, without relieving the caller of the hard-to-remember slug.

The flag accepts the exact directory name, and also a bare milestone number (digits only, zero-padded or not). A bare number resolves to the one `milestone_<NN>_*` directory whose zero-stripped number equals the value's, compared the way `goto-next-milestone` compares numbers. Path forms with a `milestones/` prefix or trailing slash are not accepted. A user or headless chain can name a milestone as `--milestone 50` without knowing its truncated slug. Numbers are unique and monotone because `define-milestone-goal` refuses a taken number, so the lookup is deterministic and fits the way milestones are already discussed and ordered. It adds the one form `capture-milestone-principle-updates` explicitly rules out ("no number-to-directory resolution exists"), so the stated exception and the uniform rule read differently on the same `<milestone_id>` placeholder. It also puts a directory-listing and matching rule into runtime prose that is followed by agents rather than a tool. That rule needs its own failure cases: a number that matches no directory, or a hand-made directory that collides with an existing number. What the existence test then checks on the resolved directory belongs to a sibling question.

The flag accepts the exact directory name, the same name with a leading `milestones/` and/or trailing slash stripped, and a bare milestone number (zero-padded or not). The number resolves to the one `milestone_<NN>_*` directory with that zero-stripped number. All three forms normalize to one `milestones/<directory name>/` before the existence check. Every way a person naturally names a milestone works: the number, the directory name, or the path shown in the pointer line. This makes the override as forgiving as possible for hand-typed invocations and for chains that know only the number. It carries both the path-stripping rule and the number-lookup rule, with their separate failure cases, in prose every resolving runner follows, and it has the widest gap from `capture-milestone-principle-updates`' verbatim positional id. That widens the exception the goal keeps and makes `<milestone_id>` mean different things in the two places the skill reference spells it.

open-question.question: Where is the rule for recognizing a leading `--milestone <milestone_id>` in a skill's invocation text and separating it from the skill's own positional text stated: once in the shared pointer procedure that every pointer-resolving skill's step 0 already references, or in each skill's own file?

Does every skill under the uniform resolution rule show the optional `--milestone <milestone_id>` flag in its own Usage block and in its `docs/skill-reference.md` heading, or is the flag documented once in one general statement while each skill's invocation form stays as it reads today?

What does the check that a named `--milestone` override matches a milestone directory actually test: that the directory exists under `milestones/`, or that its `requirements.md` exists, which is the test both positional-id skills apply today?

What does the error line for a `--milestone` override that matches no milestone directory carry beyond naming the value it was given: nothing more, the `milestone_*` directories present (as `capture-milestone-principle-updates` prints today), or a pointer to `/define-milestone-goal` (as `specify-milestone-starting-state` prints today)?

When no `--milestone` override is given and the milestone comes from the pointer in `milestones/README.md`, does the shared procedure apply to the pointer's path the same existence check it applies to an override, or does it keep trusting the pointer's path unchecked as it does today?
open-question.alternative: The pointer's path stays unchecked, as `get-current-milestone.md` handles it today: the procedure extracts the backtick-quoted path and hands it on as `<MILESTONE_DIR>` with no existence test, and the existence check runs only on a `--milestone` override. A pointer naming a missing directory is caught downstream, by the first tool call's `Error: <path> does not exist` line or by the skill's own failed file read. Keeps the default path exactly as it behaves today in all sixteen pointer-resolving skills, adding no step to the common case; the pointer is written only by `goto-next-milestone` and `finish-current-milestone`, so it rarely goes stale, and the three tools already refuse a missing document with a verbatim `Error:` line. The two resolution routes behave differently on the same fault: a bad override stops at step 0 with one error line, while a stale pointer surfaces later and in a different form per skill (a tool's `Error:` line naming a file path, or a prose read failure in skills that call no tool first, such as `ask-in-milestone-context` or `discuss-open-question`), which weakens the milestone's goal of one uniform resolution rule.

The procedure applies to the pointer's path exactly the existence check it applies to an override, and a pointer path that fails it stops on the same error line an unmatched override produces, with no fallback, so step 0 has one validation and one failure form whichever route supplied the milestone. Fully uniform: one check and one error line stated once in `get-current-milestone.md`, every skill fails at step 0 the same way on a missing milestone whatever its source, and no skill reaches a half-run state on a stale pointer. The shared error line is worded for a value the user typed, so for a stale pointer it may misdirect the user toward the invocation rather than `milestones/README.md`; how well it fits depends on what the override error carries and what the override check tests, which the "Unmatched-override error content" and "Override existence test" questions settle. It also adds a check to every default-path run.

The procedure applies to the pointer's path the same existence check it applies to an override, but a pointer path that fails it stops on its own error line, naming the path as read from the `Current milestone:` line of `milestones/README.md` and saying the pointer is stale, rather than the override's unmatched-value line. Fails every skill at step 0 on a stale pointer, as with an override, while telling the user where the bad value actually lives, so the remedy (fix the pointer or run `/finish-current-milestone`) is not confused with retyping a flag. Adds a second error wording to the shared procedure, so the two routes share a test but not a failure form, and it is one more line to keep in step with the override error as the "Unmatched-override error content" question settles it; it also adds a check to every default-path run.
